newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian phone, postal unions say strike continues.
newsitem.headline: Indian phone, postal unions say strike continues.

text.p: Indian phone and postal workers decided on Friday to continue a three-day nationwide strike until the centre-left government bows to their demands, a trade union leader said.

"The strike will continue," R.K. Kohli, assistant general secretary of the National Federation of Telecom Employees, told Reuters following a meeting of six unions leading the work stoppage by more than one million government employees.
Earlier on Friday, the federation's general secretary, O.P. Gupta, and a senior government official said they expected the strike to be called off soon, perhaps later in the day.

But Kohli said the six unions -- three representing telecommunications workers, three others in the postal sector -- agreed government assurances that their complaint would be taken up by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet were not adequate.
The unions have demanded the elimination of a ceiling on annual bonus payments, arguing that a cap on bonuses for railway workers had already been lifted.

"The decision has been taken to continue the strike until a cabinet decision," Kohli said. Deve Gowda was travelling in northeastern India and not expected back in the capital until next week. A cabinet meeting was tentatively set for next Tuesday.
